Definition: from G4166; to tend as a shepherd of (figuratively, superviser):--feed (cattle), rule.
BiblicalUsage: Poimaino means to shepherd, to feed and tend a flock. Peter tells the elders to feed the flock of God in 1 Peter 5:2, and Paul charges the Ephesian elders to feed the church of God in Acts 20:28. Jesus tells Peter, Feed my sheep, in John 21:16, and the Lamb shall feed them in Revelation 7:17. The child who is to rule all nations with a rod of iron is shepherded in Revelation 12:5.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe shepherding is feeding, not driving — the shepherd's hands are full of food, not a stick. That is why I hold that the church is fed by men who first let the Lamb feed them.
